market_commentary:
Crude oil retreated into the Canadian oil-sands breakeven band while equities held flat since the last edition — WTI crude fell to $75.43/bbl, down 6.4% from the prior edition's baseline32, settling inside the $74-76 breakeven cluster the cross-reference engine cites for 91 active oil and gas projects ($63.2B)32. The S&P/TSX Composite traded at 34,969, up 0.1%, and the S&P 500 stood at 7,501, up 0.5% over the same span32. The Canadian dollar eased 1.3% to 0.7066 CAD/USD as the Bank of Canada's overnight rate held at 2.25% following its June 10 decision1. The database tracks 6,485 active capital projects valued at $1,620.8B32.

Pipeline exposure splits along rate and commodity lines — 1,862 active rate-sensitive construction projects ($284.2B) finance against the Government of Canada curve, anchored by the 5-year benchmark at 3.04%, the mortgage-renewal reference1. If WTI holds at or below the $74-76 band, the 91 oil and gas projects ($63.2B) would sit at the lower edge of their cited breakevens32. Copper eased 2.0% since the last edition to $6.38/lb, while remaining 35.6% above its year-ago level, against 551 active mining projects ($199.9B)32.
